title: Work that follows from a result Daniel accepted reaches him only when it is a question with a recommended answer
tier_reason: changes how follow-ups are filed; git reverts it
ask:
Build the spawn rule (S-17, docs/QUEUE_TO_ZERO.md §5) in hq/work.py _file_follow_ups and _parse_follows: a follow-up with no tier is tier 1, never 2; a tier-2 follow-up is filed as a decision to prep (a card in a new `prepping` state owned by the follow-up's owner, whose result must carry `recommend` with question, answer, why, instead before it may enter needs_approval); a follow-up whose owner and normalised title match an open card merges into it (append the ask, record `merged_from`); a child carries `promised_by` = the parent card so a landed result that matches its promise never returns; snapshot()'s waiting_on_you counts only for_review and needs_approval cards that carry a recommendation. Tests for each rule.

findings.what: Merge targets include finished cards: any card not accepted/dropped is a merge candidate, so a follow-up can be appended to a for_review, needs_approval or owed card whose worker run is over — the appended ask is never read and the work is silently lost. The four open 'Read Daniel's hand edit to Obstacle Set' cards are exactly this case: wcdd64247df8 is owned by ingrid and is in for_review, so it
findings.where: hq/work.py:_file_follow_ups (open_cards = items whose state not in CLOSED_STATES)
findings.fix: Restrict merge targets to states that can still act on an appended ask — doing, waiting_session, prepping — and file a fresh card otherwise. Add a test that a follow-up matching a for_review card files rather than merges.

findings.what: A restart burns a prep attempt: _process_prep increments prep_attempts and saves before running the CLI, and _sanitize clears started without restoring the count. The token-limit branch restores it; the crash path does not, so three restarts leave a card one short draft from being declared un-writable by the studio.
findings.fix: Increment prep_attempts when a draft comes back short rather than when the run starts, or have _sanitize decrement it for prepping cards it resets.

findings.what: The prep prompt tells the seat 'this card IS the work, and it starts when he says yes' — true only because a needs_approval card shows the Approve button (waiting_session), not Accept. If anyone later makes a prepped card render as finished work (it carries result and finished), his yes would close it and the work would never run.
findings.fix: No change needed now; worth a line in the card for rin so the new prepping lane keeps needs_approval on the approve button rather than the accept one.

result:
Both HQ test files are green, the game's unit suite is green at 2,853 passing, and the diff is three files.

**What changed since last time.** The hand-back work landed in `hq/work.py` while my earlier attempt was running, so the four rules are re-applied on top of what is now on main; the behaviour he read about is unchanged, and the diff is confined to `hq/work.py`, its tests, and one paragraph in the queue plan.

**What it now does.** Follow-ups filed off a card obey the rule Daniel settled on 20 September.

A follow-up that names no tier is tier 1, never 2. An unnamed tier used to default to "ask first", which spent his attention on the model's silence.

A follow-up that is hard to walk back no longer lands in his queue as a bare ask. It files in a new state, `prepping`, owned by the seat named on it, and the read-only worker has that seat write the question: the choice in his terms, the two or three real options, what each costs, what it would take to undo each, and a recommended answer. The card may ask him for a yes only once the recommendation carries all four parts — the question, the answer, the one reason that decides it, and the alternative he might prefer. A draft that comes back short stays with the studio, says on the card what it is short of, and is written again; after three short drafts it stops looping and says a person has to write this one.

A follow-up whose owner and subject match an open card joins that card instead of filing a twin: the ask is appended and the card records which card it came from. Capitals, punctuation and a leading article are not part of the subject, so "Record the crow landing" and "The Record the crow landing." are one card. A result that names the same work twice in one block now files one card.

Every follow-up filed on his acceptance records which card promised it, and what was promised, so the landing bar being built alongside this can tell a result that does what was promised from one that differs. A follow-up an owner files from a conversation records no promise, because he never accepted it.

And the count of what waits on him counts only finished work and asks that carry a recommended answer. Measured against the cards in the repository this morning: 41 in his list, 21 of them with a recommendation, so that count reads 21. The other 20 still show on the page with their buttons, and the snapshot carries their number separately so they are uncounted rather than missing.

Tests cover each rule: the tier default and a tier that is not a number, the prepping state and its owner, a short prep and an exhausted one, a complete one entering his queue, merging by subject, not merging across owners or into a closed card, the same work named twice in one block, the promise recorded on acceptance and absent from a conversation, and the count.

**Three things he should know.** The Work page has no section for a question being written up, so a tier-2 follow-up is out of sight for the minute its question takes to draft — and stays out of sight if three attempts fail. The phrase "waiting on you" is worked out three more times in `hq/server.py` — the nightly reading of the "nothing waits on Daniel overnight" goal, the age of the oldest item, and the dashboard's own line — all of which still count every card, so the page and the dashboard will disagree until those follow. And four cards open right now all ask Ingrid to read the same hand edit to the obstacle set: the merge rule prevents the fifth, but it does not reach back and collapse the four. All three are filed below.

One smaller thing I did not file: `tools/capture_window_view.gd.uid` is the only script identity file in `tools/` missing from the repository, so every machine generates a different one. It belongs in the next commit that touches that script, not in this card's diff.

recommend.question: Apply the new rule to the queue you already have, or only to work filed from now on?
recommend.answer: Apply it to what is already there — send the 20 cards with no recommended answer back to their owners to be written as questions, and collapse the four duplicates.
recommend.why: Twenty of the 41 cards in your list ask you to rule cold, which is the exact thing the rule exists to stop, and leaving them means your queue is unchanged for weeks.
recommend.instead: Leave the existing queue alone and let the rule bite only on new work — fewer cards move under you, and you rule cold on the 20 as they come up.
